claims.statement: F.E.A.R.'s character AI uses a finite state machine with only three states - Goto, Animate and UseSmartObject - where UseSmartObject is a data-driven specialisation of Animate, leaving effectively two states, and goal-directed behaviour comes from a planner rather than from more states.
F.E.A.R. uses Goal-Oriented Action Planning: A* searches a graph whose nodes are world states and whose edges are actions, with a cost per action added to STRIPS so the planner prefers cheaper plans.

The F.E.A.R. world state is a fixed-size array of four-byte values, which limits an AI to reasoning about one weapon and one target at a time; attention-selection subsystems outside the planner choose the focus.

F.E.A.R. adds procedural preconditions and procedural effects to STRIPS so that expensive checks such as 'is there a path to safety' run only on demand, and so that action effects are not instantaneous.

Valve's Left 4 Dead AI Director is documented with explicit timing constants: the Relax period maintains a minimal threat population for 30-45 seconds or until intensity decays, and the Director creates or destroys population as the team advances.
Valve's slides state the Sustain Peak phase continues the full threat population for 3-5 seconds after Survivor Intensity has peaked, before switching to the minimal Relax population.

game_examples.fact: Jeff Orkin's GDC 2006 paper states the FSM has only three states, that A* plans sequences of actions as well as paths, and that a global coordinator periodically re-clusters AI into squads that may execute zero or one squad behaviour at a time.
game_examples.non_transferable: F.E.A.R.'s planning assumes a single-weapon, single-target fixed-size world state and a level built from cover nodes; that constraint does not transfer to an open-world or systemic-simulation game.

game_examples.fact: Mike Booth's slides describe the AI Director estimating each Survivor's emotional intensity, tracking the maximum across all four Survivors, and modulating the Infected population through Build Up, Sustain Peak, Peak Fade and Relax phases.
game_examples.locator: slides on Survivor Intensity and the Director phases
game_examples.non_transferable: The Director's intensity model is tuned for a four-player corridor shooter with discrete safe rooms; the 30-45 s Relax and 3-5 s Sustain Peak constants should not be reused for a different pacing model.

claims.statement: Flow field tiles solve crowd pathfinding by replacing per-agent A* paths with shared fields: a cost field, an integration field and a flow field, where the integration field stores integrated cost-to-goal and the flow field stores path goal directions.
claims.locator: sections 23.1-23.4 on the three field types

claims.statement: The chapter states the technique moves hundreds to thousands of individual agents across massive maps, and that agents move instantly despite path complexity because individual paths are not rebuilt per agent.

The cost field is an 8-bit field with values 0-255 where 255 marks a wall, and a shared static clear cost field is referenced when a sector is clear, so memory is only spent on sectors that carry cost.

The integration field is 24-bit (16-bit integrated cost plus 8 bits of flags such as pathable and has line of sight), and the chapter notes you can spend more memory on a 32-bit float integrated cost for better flow results.

Path requests first run A* through a portal node graph; a 'merging' A* variant prefers to stop and point to a previously travelled portal node so sources share flow-field results and path closer together.
claims.locator: section on path requests and merging A*

claims.statement: F.E.A.R.'s paper documents A* used for both navigation (nodes are navmesh polygons) and planning (nodes are world states), with a navigational path search followed by a plan search when an AI must overcome an obstacle on that path.

game_examples.fact: The Game AI Pro chapter states that in Supreme Commander 2 roughly 50-70% of pathable space was marked clear and referenced a shared static clear cost field, and that the previous one-track A* pathfinding limited the entire user experience.
game_examples.locator: chapter sections on cost fields and the Supreme Commander history
game_examples.non_transferable: The 50-70% clear-space figure comes from one RTS map population; it is not a general pathfinding memory budget and should not be copied.

game_examples.fact: The GDC 2006 paper states A* is used to find paths through the navigational mesh as well as to plan action sequences, and that when an AI crawls under an obstacle it first searches for a navigational path and then for a plan to overcome the obstacle.
game_examples.non_transferable: F.E.A.R.'s navmesh and cover-node density are tuned for small indoor combat spaces; the same node budget does not transfer to a large open world.

claims.statement: Lightmass creates lightmaps with complex light interactions such as area shadowing and diffuse interreflection, and precomputes the lighting contribution of lights with stationary and static mobility.

Epic states Lightmass emits photons based on the size of the level, so background meshes greatly increase the number of photons emitted and lengthen lighting build times; the Lightmass Importance Volume confines photon emission to the area that needs detailed indirect lighting.
Areas outside the importance volume receive only one bounce of indirect lighting at lower quality, so importance-volume placement is the direct quality-versus-build-time lever.

Baked foliage lighting is generated per instance by Lightmass and tiled per precomputed batch, and Epic warns Lightmass is less forgiving with instanced meshes, with incorrect settings producing black meshes after a lighting rebuild.
Unreal's Path Tracer is documented as sharing the ray-tracing architecture with GPU Lightmass, making it usable as a ground-truth comparison for baked lighting.

claims.statement: UnrealBuildTool manages the process of building Unreal Engine source code across a variety of build configurations, and reads user-configurable options from BuildConfiguration.cs.

Unreal is split into many modules, each with a .build.cs file controlling how it is built, including module dependencies, additional libraries and include paths; by default modules compile into DLLs loaded by a single executable, with a monolithic executable available as an option.
Epic states the build process executes independently of any project, so build configuration and project content are separate cost domains.
Unity's Build Settings control target platform, the scene list and build options, which determine what is included in a player build.

claims.statement: Ubisoft's GDC 2015 talk describes a technique of AI level of detail that allowed thousands of replicated, persistent, interactive NPCs in Assassin's Creed Unity, using a pooling system that swaps low-resolution NPCs for high-resolution NPCs without the player noticing.
The same GDC abstract states that with a limit of 40 real AIs and 120 high-resolution models, Ubisoft could create a scene with 10,000 crowd NPCs on screen at the same time.

The Unity abstract describes the crowd AI as a simplistic AI brain used to animate the thousands of NPCs, so the crowd budget is dominated by the small number of fully simulated AIs plus the animation cost of the pooled masses.

Flow-field-tile pathfinding is documented as the technique that lets hundreds to thousands of agents share path data instead of each rebuilding a path, which is the standard way to keep crowd movement affordable.

Unreal's MassEntity framework is Epic's data-oriented framework whose primary data structure is the Fragment, an atomic piece of data such as Transform, Velocity or LOD Index, grouped into Entities; it is the engine-side foundation for very large agent counts.

Valve's Director model is documented as tracking the maximum emotional intensity across all four Survivors and modulating the threat population from that, which is a concrete, testable control loop for crowd pressure.

Because a Geometry Collection can be built from other Geometry Collections, fracture authoring is hierarchical, so the depth of the fracture hierarchy is an authoring and runtime cost decision.

claims.statement: Epic states that at the Epic scalability level Lumen produces around 8 ms on next-generation consoles for global illumination and reflections at 1080p internal resolution, relying on TSR to output at quality approaching native 4K.
Epic states Lumen targets 30 and 60 fps on consoles with 8 ms and 4 ms frame budgets at 1080p for GI and reflections on opaque and translucent materials and volumetric fog.

Lumen supports two ray-tracing methods: Hardware Ray Tracing, which is higher quality and enabled by default but requires dedicated GPU support and is more expensive, and Software Ray Tracing through signed distance fields, with screen traces performed first in both cases.
Enabling Lumen GI requires Generate Mesh Distance Fields, which the engine enables automatically if it is not already on, because the software ray-tracing path traces against mesh distance fields.

The Unreal Path Tracer renders an unbiased, physically correct result from the same scene and is documented as ideal for ground-truth comparisons and production renders against the real-time renderer.

claims.statement: Unreal's Virtual Shadow Maps are described as conceptually very high-resolution shadow maps with a current virtual resolution of 16k x 16k pixels, using clipmaps to raise resolution further for directional lights.

Shadow Map Ray Tracing is the sampling algorithm used with VSMs to produce plausible soft shadows and contact hardening; rays are projected and tested against the virtual shadow map rather than intersected with geometry.

Ability Tasks are a specialised Gameplay Task class that perform asynchronous work during an ability's execution and can affect execution flow by calling delegates in C++ or moving through Blueprint execution pins.

Gameplay Effects provide a method to directly modify attribute values and contain Gameplay Effect Components that determine how an effect behaves, so attributes, effects and abilities form one dependency chain.

claims.statement: Nanite is Unreal's virtualized geometry system: it uses an internal mesh format and renders pixel-scale detail and high object counts by doing work only on the detail visible on screen.

Epic states Nanite gives a multiple-orders-of-magnitude increase in geometry complexity and that frame budgets are no longer constrained by polycount, draw calls and mesh memory usage, allowing film-quality source art to be imported directly.
Nanite's data format is highly compressed and supports fine-grained streaming with automatic level of detail, so LOD transitions no longer need manual setup per mesh.
Epic states practical limits still remain for instance counts, triangles per mesh, material complexity, output resolution and performance, so Nanite is not a blanket removal of geometry budget.

Remedy reports Alan Wake 2's GPU-driven pipeline culls meshlets (smaller optimised groups of triangles extracted from a mesh) as well as whole meshes, and that this let them ship more geometric detail than before.

Virtual Shadow Maps are designed to be used with Nanite; with Nanite in a project Epic states you must either use Movable Lights or use Virtual Shadow Maps, because Nanite does not support most Stationary Light shadowing techniques.

claims.statement: Unreal Landscape heightmaps store height as 16-bit values spanning -256 to 255.992, multiplied by the import Z scale; at the default Z scale of 100 the usable range is about +/-256 m.
Epic states each Landscape section costs one draw call and each Landscape Component has a render-thread CPU cost, and recommends a maximum of 1024 Landscape Components for the largest Landscapes.

Landscape sections are limited to a maximum of 256x256 vertices and must be a power of two, because different LOD levels are stored in the texture mipmaps; using 2x2 subsections raises resolution without adding Components.

Terrain foliage is painted directly onto a Landscape or other filter-enabled Actor and its lightmaps are generated per instance then tiled per precomputed batch, so terrain lighting and vegetation lighting are coupled.

claims.statement: The cell-and-portal method divides a model into cells (polyhedral volumes of space) and portals (transparent 2D regions on cell boundaries connecting adjacent cells); cells can only see other cells through portals, so the technique computes a conservative potentially-visible set each frame.

The paper's stated motivation is that architectural models have high depth complexity and heavy occlusion, so the ratio of actually visible objects to frustum-intersecting objects is small and a visibility algorithm can exploit that to raise interactive performance.

The paper requires the model to be subdivided along occluding primitives so that cell boundaries follow walls and portals correspond to doors and windows; a model without that structure cannot be partitioned this way.
The technique computes the potentially visible set per frame by traversing only cells in that set, so the verification is whether submitted primitives drop while the visible result is unchanged.

Teller and Sequin's earlier formulation subdivides a model into rectangular cells whose boundaries coincide with major opaque surfaces, identifies non-opaque portals on cell boundaries, and uses them to form an adjacency graph connecting the cells; cell-to-cell visibility is then computed by linking pairs of cells between which unobstructed sightlines exist.

In Teller and Sequin's interactive phase, the cell containing the observer is identified each frame and the set of potentially visible cells is further reduced by culling it against the observer's view cone, producing eye-to-cell visibility; only the remaining visible cells are sent to the graphics pipeline.

Unity's built-in 3D physics supplies the rigidbody, collider and joint layer that a wheel model is built on, so vehicle behaviour inherits the engine's solver and broad-phase characteristics.

claims.statement: Unreal's Volumetric Fog computes participating media density and lighting at every point in the camera frustum to support varying densities and any number of lights affecting the fog, and is an optional part of the Exponential Height Fog component.

Volumetric Fog can be controlled globally through Exponential Height Fog for the whole scene or locally through a particle system in areas where particles spawn, and each light's contribution can be adjusted per light.

Because density and lighting are evaluated at every point in the camera frustum, the fog cost scales with frustum volume and with the number of contributing lights, not with the number of visible fog volumes.

Remedy states Alan Wake 2's fog approximates multiple light scattering, giving it a thick and realistic look, and that the studio improved pipelines to allow more fine-grained control over fog placement in the world.

Housemarque's Returnal talk is documented as covering volumetric fog driven by real-time fluid simulations, i.e. the volumetric layer is driven by a simulation that can be tuned and inspected separately.

claims.statement: Unreal's Water system creates rivers, lakes and oceans that interact with Landscape terrains using a spline-based workflow, and unifies the shading and mesh rendering pipeline with surfaces that support physics interactions and fluid simulation with gameplay.
Epic states water surfaces support gameplay-coupled fluid effects such as ripples caused by footsteps and the wake behind a moving boat.
